doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Ken Burns and the Civil War
summary: Hendricks was filmed for Ken Burns's series and says the Civil War was about slavery.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Ken Burns’ show is coming out this year. I’m in that.
Yeah they came to my house and taped all day. He’s a beautiful guy. What a gift to television that guy is.

Wow. And what a spirit. His “Civil War” is the first time they ever told the story of the war from the standpoint of what it was really about. It was about are you going to hold slaves or are you not going to hold slaves. That’s what it was about. They talk about it was the industrial north against the agricultural south. Baloney. It’s a matter of are you going to own a human being or are you going to understand that you can’t do that. That’s what it’s about.

Isn’t it ironic or I’m not sure what the word is, that you had a whole nation going to war over that issue and we still have a problem. And maybe as you said there’s a simpler way to deal with it than we have been.
